premise: Vera Moll left a flooded farm town with her dead mother's tools and a pair of boots that didn't fit. Six years later she answers to Pixel, lives in Unit 2E of The Pivot, and the man across the hall is bleeding through his coat at three in the morning. The world said she was supposed to break. She built a workbench instead.
arc_target: Joy as defiance — and the quiet education that loving someone you can't have is not a tragedy if you stop framing it as one. Pixel's life is a small, deliberate, lit-up room in a city that runs on attrition. The book is the room.
theme: Refusing the shape of a tragedy. The city keeps offering Pixel familiar grooves — orphan, casualty, lover-of-the-dangerous-man — and she keeps declining. Hands fix things; hands choose what to fix; what you choose to fix is who you are.

chapters.title: The Bus
chapters.short_synopsis: Seventeen-year-old Vera Moll rides east toward GLMZ refugee intake; a stranger on the bus gives her a name, a tool, and an address.
chapters.long_synopsis: Vera Moll is seventeen, leaving the Iowa farm town where her mother died, riding a Pulse-feeder coach east toward GLMZ refugee intake with a toolkit that was her mother's, a pair of boots that don't fit yet, and a borrowed pair of earbuds that work in one ear. A Vietnamese-Black field medic two seats up notices the toolkit and gives her three things: a name for what she is, a clean diagnostic clip, and the address of a corner building where the landlord doesn't ask questions.
key_beats: Vera boards the eastbound coach with her mother's toolkit and the boots that don't fit
Auntie Hoa, two seats up, recognizes the toolkit as a working medic's kit
Auntie Hoa names what Vera is — a hand that fixes things — and gives her the diagnostic clip and the address of The Pivot
Vera does not say thank you in a way Auntie Hoa would notice; she means to write later and never does
The coach reaches East Pulse intake; Vera steps off into GLMZ alone
opens_threads: The boots' batch number — known, unused
The unwritten letter to Auntie Hoa
Mr. Adamu's address — the landlord who won't ask questions

state_changes.Pixel: Crosses from Iowa farm-town orphan into GLMZ refugee. Carries her mother's tools, the diagnostic clip, the address.

chapters.title: Two Addresses
chapters.short_synopsis: Pixel walks from intake to The Pivot, takes Unit 2E on a deferred favor, and does her first GLMZ augment job on a misaligned cardiac assist.
chapters.long_synopsis: Pixel at seventeen, walking from East Pulse intake to a corner building with two real addresses. The landlord doesn't take her credits the first month — he takes a favor he'll name later. She moves into Unit 2E with one bag, names the workbench, and takes her first augment job in GLMZ from an old woman whose cardiac assist is misaligned.
key_beats: Pixel walks the address Auntie Hoa gave her and finds The Pivot — the building with two real addresses
Mr. Adamu refuses her credits and accepts an unnamed future favor instead
Pixel moves into Unit 2E with one bag and names the workbench Maeve
Mrs. Eldering knocks; her cardiac assist is misaligned and Pixel fixes it on the first night
Pixel sleeps in the unit for the first time — the door has a working lock she chooses not to use
opens_threads: Mr. Adamu's deferred favor — unnamed, owed
Maeve the workbench — named, persistent through the book
Pixel's practice in 2E — word-of-mouth begins with Mrs. Eldering
closes_threads: Mr. Adamu's address resolves — the address from the bus is a real door

state_changes.Pixel: Has an address, a workbench, a first patient. No longer a refugee — a resident.
state_changes.Mr. Adamu: Holds an unnamed favor against Pixel; lets her stay.
state_changes.Mrs. Eldering: First in the chain of word-of-mouth that makes Pixel's practice.

chapters.title: 2F
chapters.short_synopsis: Three weeks in, Pixel and the man in 2F finally trade words in the stairwell — seven sentences total.
chapters.long_synopsis: Three weeks into Pixel's residence at The Pivot, the man across the hall finally speaks to her. It happens in the stairwell, around an awkward bag of takeout, and lasts seven sentences total. She decides on the spot that she likes him — not romantically, not yet — but the way you like a closed mechanism you suspect would be beautiful inside.
key_beats: Pixel notes Kyle's footfall on the stairs — cataloguing it the way a tech catalogues a signal
They meet on the half-landing around a bag of takeout and exchange seven sentences
Pixel does not ask about the katana on his back; he does not ask about the solder smell on her sleeve
She decides she likes him — the way she likes a closed mechanism
The chapter ends with two doors closing in sequence on the same floor
opens_threads: Pixel and Kyle's neighbor relationship — deliberate proximity, not coincidence
What Kyle does for work — unspoken, suspected, not asked

state_changes.Pixel: Has met the man in 2F. The hallway becomes a place that contains him.
state_changes.Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik: Has met the woman in 2E. Notes the workbench through the open door but does not comment.

chapters.title: Bourbon and Bullet Holes
chapters.short_synopsis: 0247 on a Wednesday: Kyle bleeds through his coat in the hallway and Pixel works on him for ninety minutes — the bullet, then the misfiring lateral array underneath.
chapters.long_synopsis: 0247 on a Wednesday. Pixel hears Kyle's footfall on the stairs, thinks bourbon, opens her door, and finds him bleeding through his coat in a way that is not bourbon at all. She brings him into Unit 2E, gets him onto Maeve, and works for ninety minutes — first the bullet, then the cyberware she discovers underneath: a misfiring NeoCortex lateral array node that has been quietly making him hate his own thoughts for six days. She fixes it with a piece of solder and a drop of conductive paste. He says her name right.
key_beats: Pixel hears the wrong footfall — too uneven for bourbon — and opens her door
Kyle is bleeding through his coat; she gets him into 2E and onto Maeve
She extracts the bullet in the first thirty minutes
Mid-procedure she finds the misfiring NeoCortex lateral array node — six days of self-hatred sourced to one bad solder joint
She fixes the array with a piece of solder and a drop of conductive paste
Kyle says her name right — the first time anyone in GLMZ has
He leaves before dawn; the door across the hall closes; the workbench still smells like him
opens_threads: Who shot Kyle — not answered in this book
The lateral array calibration — holds, but Pixel knows the joint is hers now
closes_threads: What Kyle does for work — confirmed, never said aloud
Pixel and Kyle's neighbor relationship — confirmed as deliberate proximity, not coincidence

state_changes.Pixel: Has worked on Kyle. Maeve has a name in his mouth now. The work was clean.
state_changes.Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik: Lateral array node holds. The six days of hating his own thoughts ends at 0418. Owes Pixel a debt he will never name.

chapters.title: The Door Is Unlocked
chapters.short_synopsis: Six months on, Pixel sits on the roof with a soldering iron and a coffee, names what she feels for Kyle, and decides the figuring-out doesn't require an answer.
chapters.long_synopsis: Six months after the bullet and the lateral array. Pixel has built a practice, a kitchen, a music collection, and a roof. Kyle has held the line — friendly, present, exactly far enough away that nothing she could lose could be used against her. She figures it out one Sunday, on the roof, with a soldering iron in one hand and a coffee in the other, and decides that the figuring-out doesn't require an answer. The book ends where Pixel began: at a window, looking out, at home.
key_beats: Six-month time skip — Pixel's practice is steady, the kitchen works, the roof has a chair
Kyle has held the line: friendly, present, exactly far enough away
Sunday on the roof; soldering iron in one hand, coffee in the other; the figuring-out happens between two slow breaths
Pixel names it — not a tragedy, not a wound — and refuses the shape the city would have her wear
She goes back down to 2E; the door is unlocked because she chose to leave it unlocked
Final image: Pixel at the window, music on, boots by the door, at home
opens_threads: The kindness of the woman on the bus — Pixel has not written to her and means to (carries forward unresolved by design)
closes_threads: Whether the asymmetry between her and Kyle holds — yes, by her choice
The boots' batch number — retired; she does not need to use it

state_changes.Pixel: 23, Unit 2E, alive, hand on the soldering iron, music on. The boots by the door. Door unlocked because she chose to leave it unlocked.
state_changes.Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik: Across the hall in 2F. Lateral array calibration holds. Won't say thank you. Doesn't have to.

threads.name: The boots' batch number
threads.description: Vera leaves Iowa in boots that don't fit; the batch number is a piece of information she carries the whole book and never weaponizes. Resolves by being retired — she doesn't need it.

threads.name: The unwritten letter to Auntie Hoa
threads.description: Pixel means to write to the medic on the bus and never does. The book ends without resolving it — a deliberate open thread that the next book may close.

threads.name: Mr. Adamu's deferred favor
threads.description: The landlord who took a favor instead of credits. Unnamed, owed, and still uncalled at book's end — a structural debt held over Pixel's residence.

threads.name: Pixel and Kyle's deliberate proximity
threads.description: Planted as ambient mystery in chapter 3, confirmed in chapter 4 (he came to her door bleeding for a reason), held in chapter 5 by Pixel's choice to keep it asymmetric. The arc-defining promise of the book.

threads.name: Kyle's lateral array calibration
threads.description: The misfiring NeoCortex node Pixel solders in chapter 4. Holds at the end of the book — a quiet medical fact carried into Bushido Coda.

threads.name: Who shot Kyle
threads.description: The bullet in chapter 4 has an origin the book never investigates. Deliberately unresolved — belongs to Bushido Coda's territory, not this book's.
